## What this is

Open EP Mapping Lab (published at [openepengineering.org]({{< var site.url >}}), Open EP Engineering) is a free, open
course on how cardiac electroanatomic mapping systems work: how they locate catheters, record and process electrograms,
and build activation and voltage maps. It is written for engineers joining electrophysiology (EP) device companies,
clinical mapping specialists and field engineers, EP fellows and physicians who want the engineering view, and
researchers who use open EP tools. The course has 55 modules in eight parts; the [course map](course-map.qmd) lists them
all.

## Who makes it

The course is created and maintained by its author: connect on [LinkedIn]({{< var author.linkedin >}}), or see
[raghavendrasri](https://github.com/raghavendrasri) on GitHub. All of its source, including every page, test and
lab, is public in the [course repository]({{< var repo.url >}}).

## How the content is written and checked

The site and its drafts are developed with AI assistants, Claude (Anthropic) and Gemini (Google), and checked against
written rules before they are published:

- **Equations:** every equation has a numeric test in code, and a symbolic check where feasible.
- **Numbers:** every value comes from a cited source or from the course's own code. Where a source is missing, the
  value is marked and kept out of releases.
- **Citations:** every reference is looked up and stored with its DOI or PubMed ID.
- **Figures:** every figure is labeled as exact, simulation, approximate model or schematic, with its assumptions
  listed.
- **Human review:** nothing is marked reviewed until a person signs it off. Clinical sections stay "pending clinical
  review" until an EP physician approves them. Sign-offs are recorded publicly in the repository.

**Current status:** all 55 modules are drafts. None has been reviewed yet, so treat every page as a draft. Corrections
are listed on the [Errata](errata.qmd) page.

## What it is not

Education only. The course is not for diagnosis, treatment or any clinical decision. It gives no ablation-strategy
advice and no vendor operating instructions. Product names are used only to describe products, from public sources, and
mentioning a company or product is not an endorsement. See the [Disclaimer](disclaimer.qmd).

## Built on and credits

- [OpenEP](https://github.com/openep) for mapping data formats and analysis
- [openCARP](https://www.opencarp.org/) for cardiac simulation
- [PhysioNet](https://physionet.org/) and [EDGAR](https://edgar.sci.utah.edu/) for public recordings
- The course format (parts, modules, live figures, code labs) is inspired by
  [OpenUltrasoundLab](https://openultrasoundlab.org). Only the idea is borrowed; no text, figures or code.

Open EP Mapping Lab is an independent educational project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by the
[OpenEP](https://openep.io/) project or any medical device manufacturer.

## How to cite {#how-to-cite}

Please cite the whole course as:

> Open EP Mapping Lab contributors. 2026. "Open EP Mapping Lab: An Open Course on Cardiac Electroanatomic Mapping
> Systems." https://openepengineering.org/.

```bibtex
@online{openepmappinglab2026,
  author = {{Open EP Mapping Lab contributors}},
  title = {Open {EP} Mapping Lab: An Open Course on Cardiac
           Electroanatomic Mapping Systems},
  year = {2026},
  url = {https://openepengineering.org/}
}
```

Pages change as the course grows, so add the date you read it (`urldate` in BibTeX). To cite a single module, use the
**Citation** box at the bottom of that page. The course repository's **Cite this repository** button on GitHub gives
the same citation, from its `CITATION.cff` file.

## Page views and privacy {#privacy}

The site counts page views with Cloudflare Web Analytics, so the author can see which pages are read. According to
Cloudflare, it uses no cookies or other storage in your browser and does not fingerprint visitors. The counter loads
only on openepengineering.org, and not at all if your browser sends a Global Privacy Control or Do Not Track signal.
The site stores nothing else about you; your light or dark choice is kept only in your own browser.

## License and contact

Text, figures and questions are licensed [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); code is
licensed MIT. Datasets keep their original licenses, self-hosted IBM Plex fonts are under the SIL Open Font License 1.1,
and the project logo is reserved to identify Open EP Mapping Lab.

Found an error or have a suggestion? Use the **Feedback** button at the bottom right of any page, or open an
issue in the [course repository]({{< var repo.url >}}/issues). Feedback is posted publicly as a GitHub issue,
together with the page's address and, if you choose, the text you selected. The form does not collect your name,
email or IP address, so please don't include personal or patient information. It uses Cloudflare Turnstile to keep
out spam bots, loaded only when you open the form. When automatic sending is not available, the button opens a
prefilled issue on GitHub instead, which you post with your own GitHub account.
